question: What is the main effect of giving opioids to a woman in labour?

options.A: Lowering the mother's blood pressure by constricting major blood vessels
options.B: Altering pain perception within the central nervous system
options.C: Permanently stopping all uterine contractions during the first stage
options.D: Speeding up cervical dilation by relaxing the pelvic floor muscles

explanation: Opioids act mainly on the central nervous system to change how the brain perceives painful stimuli during labour. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why must a midwife be careful when giving an opioid close to delivery?

options.A: The drug easily crosses the placenta and can cause breathing problems in the newborn
options.B: It causes immediate and permanent high blood pressure in the postpartum period
options.C: It will completely stop the mother from pushing during the second stage of labour
options.D: The newborn baby will experience severe bone pain right after birth

explanation: Opioids cross the placenta easily, meaning a dose given too close to delivery can suppress the baby's breathing at birth. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which specific receptor type is mainly responsible for pain relief and slowed breathing from opioids?
explanation: Mu receptors are the main binding sites that produce both the desired pain relief and the side effect of slowed breathing. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h2)

question: A mother complains of severe constipation two days after receiving an opioid. What causes this?

options.A: Opioids decrease bowel motility and slow down peristalsis in the gut
options.B: Opioids block the brain from recognizing when the rectum is full
options.C: The drug causes permanent damage to the muscular lining of the large intestine
options.D: The medication forces the body to absorb all water from solid waste instantly

explanation: Opioid binding in the gastrointestinal tract slows down normal bowel movements, leading to sluggish digestion and constipation. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h2)

question: What essential emergency drug must be nearby before giving morphine?
explanation: Naloxone is the specific opioid antagonist used to reverse dangerous respiratory depression caused by morphine. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is morphine usually avoided when a woman is very close to giving birth?

options.A: It increases the risk that the newborn will have a depressed respiratory effort at birth
options.B: It stops breast milk production for the first three days following delivery
options.C: It permanently stops the uterus from contracting during the transitional phase
options.D: It makes the mother completely allergic to local anaesthetics used for episiotomies

explanation: Giving morphine close to delivery gives the drug too little time to clear before birth, increasing the chance the baby will struggle to breathe. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the breakdown product of pethidine that can build up and affect the nervous system?
explanation: Norpethidine is a byproduct broken down by the body that has a long half-life and can stimulate the nervous system, potentially causing tremors or seizures. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why do the effects of pethidine sometimes last longer in newborns?

options.A: The amniotic fluid traps the drug and forces the baby to swallow it repeatedly
options.B: Breast milk immediately re-concentrates the pethidine back into the baby's stomach
options.C: Pethidine permanently binds to the baby's skin cells and is released very slowly
options.D: The baby's immature liver and kidneys take longer to clear the drug and its active metabolite

explanation: Newborns lack fully developed organ systems to metabolize and excrete drugs efficiently, causing the active metabolites to linger. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of opioids during labour?
explanation: Opioids cause sedation, nausea, and slowed digestion, but they do not typically cause fever or chills. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why does opioid use increase the risk of aspiration if a mother needs an emergency caesarean section?

options.A: It causes the windpipe to swell shut during the induction of anaesthesia
options.B: The medication relaxes the lungs so much that they fill up with saliva
options.C: The drugs slow down stomach emptying, leaving food and liquids in the stomach longer
options.D: Opioids force the stomach to produce large amounts of thick, acidic mucus

explanation: Because opioids delay gastric emptying, stomach contents can remain high, raising the danger of inhaling vomit during anaesthesia. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h5)

question: How does naloxone work to reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: It coats the lungs with a protective layer that blocks the drug from entering
options.B: It speeds up the heart rate to force the body to sweat out the drug
options.C: It permanently destroys the opioid molecules inside the patient's bloodstream
options.D: It competitively blocks and displaces opioid molecules from the receptor sites

explanation: Naloxone attaches to the same receptors as opioids, pushing them off and temporarily blocking their action. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is close monitoring needed after giving naloxone?

options.A: Naloxone causes severe allergic reactions exactly one hour after injection
options.B: It causes the blood pressure to drop to zero without warning
options.C: The patient will immediately fall into a permanent coma once the drug takes effect
options.D: Naloxone wears off faster than many opioids, allowing breathing depression to return

explanation: Because naloxone has a short half-life, its reversal effects fade before long-acting opioids clear, risking a return of dangerous symptoms. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which vital sign measurement acts as an immediate warning sign after opioid administration?

options.A: Respiratory rate dropping below twelve breaths per minute
options.C: Blood pressure reading of 140 over 90 mmHg
options.D: Pulse rate rising above one hundred beats per minute

explanation: A slow respiratory rate below 12 breaths per minute indicates dangerous respiratory depression from the opioid. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h7)

question: A midwife is preparing to give pethidine to a mother in active labour. What is the most important safety action to complete first?

options.A: Check that resuscitation equipment and naloxone are fully ready at the bedside
options.B: Ensure the mother has eaten a heavy meal to prevent stomach irritation
options.C: Ask the doctor to prescribe long-term oral antibiotics for the postpartum period
options.D: Discharge the patient home since labour will proceed without complications

explanation: Emergency reversal tools and breathing equipment must be verified and ready before giving any opioid. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h7)
